assessments.reasoning: Mozilla's HTTP 200 media response on the cutoff date supplied the complete publisher baseline. Its independently verified 16,726 bytes and digest matched the publisher identity claim. The first mismatch and full-suffix test established which side contained the additional byte.

The HTTP 200 acquisition at 14:56:39Z on the cutoff date came from text/MPL-2.0.txt in the pinned spdx/license-list-data commit. Its complete license text reproduced the stated length and digest. Direct comparison located the extra space and excluded any second difference from Mozilla.

The separate HTTP 200 acquisition at 14:56:34Z on the cutoff date came from text/MPL-2.0-no-copyleft-exception.txt in the same commit. The body extended from the license title through Exhibit B and the final newline. Its measured length, digest, and full equality with the standard file confirmed that this distinct path carries the same additional space.

challenge.method: Verified the distinct text-directory paths and the complete ASCII byte counts. All named-range lists were empty. Compared the two generated bodies directly, then scanned the publisher and standard SPDX bodies from the beginning to locate the first mismatch without supplying an expected offset. Tested the entire remaining suffix after skipping one SPDX byte.
challenge.results: The generated files were equal to one another and unequal to Mozilla's response. In section 1.7, the SPDX byte at offset 1282 is 0x20 immediately before a line feed. The preceding 1,282 bytes and the entire suffix beginning with that line feed matched. Trimming trailing spaces would conceal the sole difference.

limitations: The two SPDX URLs identify commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, supplied as the 3.29.0 snapshot. The six acquisitions did not separately verify the release tag's mapping to that commit.
The HTTP observations fall on 2026-11-23 and identify the requested URLs. They do not identify a geographic serving location or establish behavior at other endpoints or dates.

The comparison covers the generated plaintext files. It establishes no equivalence between SPDX identifiers, project notices, headers, JSON properties, templates, rendered pages, or legal effects. Reuse rights were outside the measurement.
reasoning: The two distinct SPDX text files matched at all 16,727 byte positions. Independent SHA-256 calculations for both complete bodies reproduced the connector's reported digest, 66a3107d5ad6a058aab753eaac2047ccb2ed0e39465dd0fe5844da3e300d5172. Relative to Mozilla's 16,726-byte response, each SPDX body has exactly one additional ASCII space at zero-based byte offset 1282. The complete 1,706-byte revision 1 claim record also reproduced the supplied claim digest.

reproduction.reason: The execution directly compared the complete acquired source texts. Its native tool result matched an independent byte-level replay without normalization.
